title: Build a Mini Adventure Game
summary: Use everything you know — functions, loops, conditions, and input — to build a complete text adventure.

content.title: You Have Everything You Need
content.summary: Variables, input, if/else, loops, and functions — combined, they can build a real game.
content.body:
Here is every tool you have now:

• Variables — remember information
• input() — ask the player questions
• if / elif / else — make decisions
• for loops — repeat actions
• Functions — reusable named scenes

A text adventure game uses all five. The functions become the scenes; the loop drives the game; conditions branch the story.

content.title: A Starting Skeleton
content.summary: Define your scenes as functions, then call them in story order at the bottom.

content.title: Project Requirements
content.summary: Your game must use at least 3 functions, 1 loop, 1 if/else, and 1 input().
content.body:
Your adventure game must include:

- At least 3 functions (scenes or actions)
- At least 1 for loop (a battle, a search, a countdown)
- At least 1 if/else (a choice that changes what happens)
- At least 1 input() (ask the player something)
- A clear beginning, middle, and end

Think about your story first. What is the setting? What is the challenge? How does it end?

content.title: Plan Before You Code
content.summary: Write your scene names on paper first — then build one function at a time.
content.body:
Before writing a single line, answer these:

• What are my 3 scenes? (name each one)
• Where does the player make a choice?
• What does the loop repeat? (battle rounds? exploration steps?)
• What question does input() ask?
• What is the final message?

Write the function names at the bottom first, then fill each one in from top to bottom.

editorPrompt: Build your mini adventure game. At least 3 functions, 1 loop, 1 if/else, and 1 input(). Start by writing the function names and the calls at the bottom — then fill each function in.
starterCode:
# Mini Adventure Game — Final Project
# Plan your scenes first:
#   - What are your 3 functions?
#   - Where is the player choice (if/else)?
#   - What does the loop repeat?
#   - What does input() ask?

def intro():
    pass

def challenge():
    pass

def ending():
    pass

# Call your scenes in order
intro()
challenge()
ending()
progressiveHints: Start with intro(): just 2–3 print lines setting the scene. Replace pass and call it to make sure it works.
Build challenge() next. Add an input() for a player decision and an if/else that branches on their answer.
Add a for loop inside challenge() — battle rounds, search steps, or a countdown.
Fill in ending() last. Make it feel like a proper conclusion — reference what the player did if you can.
challenge: Add a score variable that increases based on the player's choices and how the battle goes. Print the final score in ending().
